subject: Troubleshooting Multi-species distance sampling using Point count data

messages.author: d1e5472b4d6f87f3
messages.subject: Troubleshooting Multi-species distance sampling using Point count data
parts:
Hi everyone!

I write here to you in urgent need of help regarding the analysis of the multi-species point count data using distance sampling. I am using distance sampling approach as discussed in this paper paper: https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1365-2664.2006.01271.x
and following the methods and code used in here:  here: https://examples.distancesampling.org/Distance-spec-covar/species-covariate-distill.html#visualising-the-detection-functions-for-each-species

Aim: I want to estimate densities of birds in two habitats types (shrubland and forest). I counducted point count surveys in both the habitats. 

Method: As discussed in the aforementioned paper, I am using multi-species groups which contains detection data from birds which are similar (eg. bulbuls as one group). So, I want to estimate densities of three species of bulbuls in both shrubland and forest habitat. The dataset has detection data for three species of bulbuls. I have been able to run and use the code for one habitat but it keeps showing different errors for the forest habitat. 

Problems: 
1. The error that comes while running the density code for forest is: 
Error in predict.ds(ddf, newdata = bigdat_nona, compute = TRUE) : fields or factor levels in `newdata` do not match data used in fitted model.
I tried using this the function 'droplevels', but I am not sure why do I need to use this for this habitat data.

Note: the code is running and densities are returning just fine in the shrubland data without any error. 

2. I am also unable to understand how does the code reads NAs in the data. So, there are quite a few sampling units, where the species is not detected, however the point count (effort) was done. For those samples, I have entered effort but for object and distance I have used NAs. ( as done in this data and code https://examples.distancesampling.org/Distance-points/pointtransects-distill.html)
However, when the code reads the frequency table of detections (attached here), it also counts the frequency of NAs as detections. Please help me understand how the distance sampling treats NAs.


Attaching the R code here, please help in troubleshooting this. 

The headers for my data are:
Region.Label    Area    Sample.Label    Effort    object    distance    species    Study.Area


best, 
Yukti
